angle: Autonomous actions need spend controls and shadow-mode validation before production authority.
sourceTitle: It’s All Fun and Games Until You Give AI Your Credit Card
linkedinPost:
Letting AI act is where the real value — and real risk — starts.

The Atlantic shares consumer stories of assistants going off-script once given payment authority. Enterprises face the same pattern at higher stakes: mistaken orders, vendor sprawl, or endless loops that rack up fees.

In production, I treat agent spending like any other financial control:

• Shadow mode first: simulate actions and reconcile predicted vs. actual outcomes for 2–4 weeks.
• Role-based budgets: per-task caps, daily limits, and pre-approved vendor lists.
• Approval thresholds: auto-approve <$X, route to a human above it. Every transaction logged with rationale.
• Kill switch and rollback: one click to revoke tokens and reverse actions.

Yes, this slows you down a week. It also prevents a month of cleanup — and preserves customer trust when agents touch refunds, credits, or procurement.

What’s your minimum control set before granting agents the corporate card? #AIStrategy #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI
xPost: Autonomy without spend controls is a cleanup plan. Shadow mode, per-task budgets, approval thresholds, full audit logs, and a kill switch — or don’t give agents the card. #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
